newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Iceland braced for profit freeze.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Iceland braced for profit freeze.

text.p: British frozen food retailer Iceland Group Plc is set to reveal on Tuesday how aggressive competition from big supermarkets has sent shivers through its first half profits.
Iceland warned in July that interim profits were likely to come in 10 percent lower than last year's 33.6 million stg, blaming erratic trading.
Retail analysts predict profits of around 30 million stg, and a dividend of about 1.8 pence, up from 1.65 pence.
Iceland has said it remains cash generative and would stick to its progressive dividend policy.

The chain, which relies on frozen food for about 50 percent of its business, has suffered as intense rivalry between big stores like Tesco Plc and J. Sainsbury Plc have increased competition on price and frozen food ranges.
Analysts said the introduction of loyalty cards by the major supermarkets had added to pressure on Iceland's position as a second-line retailer.
The group's stores are mainly in town centres, while many of the superstores' outlets are out of town.
The advent of loyalty cards means people are more likely to buy frozen food at their major superstore rather than make a separate trip to Iceland, said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
"The loyalty techniques of the majors mean secondary shopping is not as popular," he added.
Iceland has always billed itself as a niche player, but analysts say the new loyalty schemes and the other competitive pressures are challenging its position.
The shares were hit badly by July's profit warning but have since fallen further to stand at 106 pence, down from a high earlier this year of 162 pence.
"The shares look cheap, but we're still sellers as we don't see any immediate recovery," said retail analyst Bill Myers at Williams de Broe.
